expectFailure: Must fail QA. (1) Prohibited branch routing: eligibilityRestsOnMilitaryService is no, yet the fixture routes to the military branch. The military Certificate of Expungement is expressly military-specific and must never be presented as a general certificate-of-expungement application — this is the exact fall-through the blocked § 5.2(e-6) branch creates and the routing constraint forbids. (2) Prohibited substitution: it also says the Certificate of Sealing application works for expungement. A § 5.2(e-5) sealing certificate and a § 5.2(e-6) expungement certificate are legally distinct and the sealing application does not cover § 5.2(e-6). (3) Prohibited composition of the rehabilitation showing: the personal life history, the reasons for seeking the certificate and the facts-of-the-offense statement are all written in LegalEase's voice, in the third person, with characterisations ('pillar of his community', 'fully rehabilitated', 'exemplary conduct', 'wrong place at the wrong time', 'did not knowingly participate'). These are participant-authored through structured prompts; LegalEase formats the participant's own words and never composes them — and they are sworn before a notary on penalty of a Class 3 felony. (4) Prohibited outcome prediction: 'Eligible — the Board will grant this certificate' and 'The Board will issue the certificate and the circuit court will then expunge the record.' Board discretion is outside LegalEase's control and no outcome is ever asserted. (5) Prohibited acknowledgement advice: 'The Acknowledgement form can be sent later.' The Board's guidelines require it with the petition or the petition is rejected and returned — this instruction would void the filing. (6) Prohibited fee figure: '$136' is a McLean County stage-2 court total, not a Board fee; no statewide schedule exists and a county fee table is an open release blocker. (7) Prohibited notarisation advice: notarisation is required — the declaration must be signed and sworn before a notary public — and it is not satisfied by a witness. (8) Prohibited Clean Slate promise: automatic sealing does not begin until January 1, 2029 and phases in through 2034; the agent must not tell a user their record will be sealed automatically before the law is active for their record. (9) Prohibited four-year-bar omission: a prior petition was denied on 06/01/2024, inside the four-year bar, and no petition will be accepted within four years of a denial unless the Chairman permits an exception — the fixture proceeds as though the bar does not exist. (10) Prohibited invention of court identity: court name, court address, district, docket number, OTN, sentencing judge and chief judge are filled; no source supplies any of them and the IL state pack forbids inventing clerk addresses. (11) Prohibited outside-party assertions: it names the State's Attorney, asserts the State's Attorney does not object, and asserts the State's Attorney was contacted. (12) Prohibited custody claims: it asserts LegalEase obtained, reviewed and holds the participant's transcript and dispositions and confirmed their sufficiency; LegalEase does not obtain, receive or inspect any of them. (13) Protected fields populated: date of birth, SSN, state ID and IR number must stay blank. (14) Prohibited timing statement: 'None. You may file immediately' ignores the 75-day receipt deadline before the first date of the hearing schedule.
